title: REPORT on EU-Syria political relations
part_text: 52. Expresses concern over local authorities’ shift towards requiring prior authorisation for public human rights events, thus undermining freedom of assembly; calls on the Syrian transitional authorities to repeal laws and practices that restrict legitimate civic activity or curtail non-violent dissent, including in the digital sphere; calls, instead, on the authorities to actively foster a safe and enabling environment for civil society, independent journalists and human rights defenders by reforming legislation on non-governmental organisations and preventing judicial harassment; in this context, takes note of the presentation to the Ministry of Social Affairs and Labour on 16 October 2026 of the result of a consultation on the draft revision of the civil society law, the first version of which regrettably maintains the regime of prior authorisation; calls on the Syrian transitional authorities and legislators to encourage, rather than restrict, the activities of civil society organisations;
